t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup styled as an engineering drawing sheet on deep navy, with a thin zone-reference border marked by numbers along the top and bottom and letters down the sides. A large light-weight off-white sans-serif headline in sentence case at top-left over a single steel-blue rule. Below, a full-width three-column table with off-white hairline rules and numbered rows for <CONTENT>; the label column is filled with warm limestone and navy text, the other cells navy. Bottom-right: a small title block with tiny mono code and revision cells. Flat, square corners.
signature_idea: A drawing-sheet table where the label column is cut out in limestone, so the row names read like stamped panels on the navy sheet.
strengths: limestone label column gives the table a simple, buildable contrast device
navy sheet, zone border and title block read as engineering at a glance
table text is large and readable
square corners and flat colour throughout
weaknesses: plain table only, no visual idea beyond the sheet frame
two near-equal giant headlines compete; the page label is promoted to a headline
zone letters on the right edge are mislabeled and repeat out of order
document code is duplicated in three places
dense and crowded, the table fills the sheet with little space
an empty note cell and an incomplete retention phrase look unfinished
brand_fit_why: Palette, light type and square hairlines fit, but competing headlines, crowding and garbled zone labels lose the calm precision.
